mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in UNRATE, predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate tighter financial conditions.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in >70% of triggered events, or FEDFUNDS increase is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be positive as market anticipates stronger economic momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to baseline (p > 0.05) in 80% of such events, or the momentum signal decays within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS (labor market employment) by more than 1% month-over-month predicts a positive S&P 5-day forward return as hiring momentum is interpreted as economic strength.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of triggered events, or employment growth is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below its 4-quarter moving average, especially when accompanied by a rising CPIAUCSL (inflation), predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns as weak manufacturing and rising costs erode profit expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of such events, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods where FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent rate hikes dampening equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such episodes, or FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for the subsequent 6 months without a reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST (housing starts) by at least 10% over the prior three months is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it signals renewed construction activity and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > prev(HOUST) AND HOUST[month-2] <= prev(HOUST) AND (HOUST - prev(HOUST)) / prev(HOUST) >= 0.10
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to baseline (p > 0.05) in 75% of such events, or the trend reverses within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is more likely to be positive as lower unemployment is interpreted as a labor market recovery.
regime_hint: labor market softening turning to strength
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of such events, or the UNRATE decline is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both INDPRO and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% month-over-month predicts negative S&P 5-day forward returns as dual softness in manufacturing and retail erodes demand outlook.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev(INDPRO) AND RSAFS < prev(RSAFS) AND (INDPRO - prev(INDPRO)) / prev(INDPRO) <= -0.02 AND (RSAFS - prev(RSAFS)) / prev(RSAFS) <= -0.02
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >70% of triggered events, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
